To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) soil quality indicators are sensitive to short-term changes in the physical, chemical, and biological soil properties; (2) soil quality indicators can be used to detect changes in soil properties and processes; (3) soil bulk density should be expressed on a volume basis; and (4) soil quality indicator values should be expressed on an areal basis to allow for comparisons between systems and across dates.

the soil quality assessment approach we have used is capable of detecting rapid changes in soil quality, but the approach is limited by the lack of specific guidelines for interpreting results and by the need to carefully select sampling locations and consider soil bulk density in all soil property assessments.

soil quality indicators are sensitive to rapid changes in soil properties and processes that occur by soil management, but the interpretation and use of these indicators is difficult because of the lack in the literature of specific criteria for interpreting results.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a better understanding of the capacity of soil quality indicators to assess soil conditions and processes and to determine their ability to detect short term changes in soil quality as influenced by tillage and residue practices.
the development of soil quality indices and their use in determining soil quality status.
the assessment of soil quality and the use of biological, chemical, and physical properties to detect short-term differences in soil conditions and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the soil quality indicators used in this study are sensitive to short-term changes in the soil environment, and can detect differences in soil conditions between systems.

the use of these soil quality indicators in this study did not provide a definitive assessment of soil quality status, but did provide a sensitive assessment of short-term changes in the soil environment that occur by the effects of soil management.

the soil property indices used in this study are sensitive to changes in soil quality, and can detect short-term changes, but the results are difficult to interpret because of the lack or limited information on the specific criteria or guidelines for interpreting the results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soil quality indices are useful to assess the short-term changes in soils that occur as a result of different soil management practices.

soil quality indices are sensitive to the detection and assessment of rapid changes in soils as affected by soil management and tillage systems, but the interpretation of results is difficult and requires careful consideration of the soil conditions and sampling location in the field.
all of the soil quality indicators studied are useful for detecting short-term changes in the status of soil function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil property indices can be used to monitor short term changes in soil quality but the interpretation of results is not as straightforward as it might seem.
soil quality indicators are sensitive to changes in soil conditions.
soil quality indices should be interpreted on a case-by-case basis and that a single index cannot be used as the sole indicator of soil quality.
